svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.23.11.3 Top Plates
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Top Plates

g.text: Loadbearing wall: at least 2 top plates, (1)
Single top plate over the lintel, forming
Single plate tied across a lintel
Single top plate: loads 50 mm or less to
Single plate, loads over the studs
No top plates over the lintel: lintel tied
to the wall on each side, (4)
No top plate at a lintel

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as permitted in Sentences (2) to (4),
at least 2 top plates are provided in
loadbearing walls.
A single top plate is permitted in a section
of a loadbearing wall containing a lintel
provided the top plate forms a tie across the
lintel.
A single top plate is permitted in loadbearing
walls where the concentrated loads from
ceilings, floors and roofs are not more than
50 mm to one side of the supporting studs, and
in all non-loadbearing walls.
The top plates need not be provided in a
section of loadbearing wall containing a
lintel provided the lintel is tied to the
adjacent wall section with not less than
(a) 75 mm by 150 mm by 0.91 mm thick galvanized
steel, or (b) 19 mm by 89 mm by 300 mm wood
splice nailed to each wall section with at least
three 63 mm nails.
Drawn: upper part of each wall only. Top plates or ties in question in yellow. In C the joists sit 30 mm off the stud centres. Sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.11.3. (page 9-185)
